title: PETITIONS AVAILABLE
full_story:
Flora City Clerk Kaci O’Dell announced that petition forms and other applicable election filing forms for the office of Mayor and Commissioners for the City of Flora will be available to interested, qualified, registered voters beginning tomorrow.  The packet of forms and pertinent information may be picked up at Flora City Hall, 131 East Second Street, Monday through Friday, between the hours of 9:00 am and 4:30 pm, with the exception of holiday closures.

Flora’s Consolidated Election, to be held on April 6th, and will be for electing a Mayor and four Commissioners.  Individuals elected will serve a 4-year term, beginning May 1st (first regular council meeting of May) through April 30, 2031.  If petitions filed total more than four for the Mayor’s position and/or more than sixteen for the Commissioners’ positions, a Consolidated Primary Election will be held on February 23rd.

Prospective candidates may start circulating petitions tomorrow.

The filing period for nonpartisan candidates is November 16th through November 23rd.

A notice will be circulated to the media as a reminder of the filing dates.

title: NORTH CLAY BOARD
full_story:
North Clay Unit District 25 board members heard an upbeat start-of-school report during their Wednesday night meeting in Louisville.

Principals Sarah Newby and Ben Borries shared positive news from across the district, including strong open house attendance at both the elementary/junior high and high school.  Hundreds attended the elementary event, with support from the PTO, Health Department, Transportation Department, school nurse, Edgewood Masonic Lodge, and Christ Church of Flora.  Enrollment stands at 388 students in Pre-K through eighth grade and 168 at North Clay High School.

The board also approved the tentative FY27 budget they also set a public hearing for September 23rd.  Superintendent Price stated that the pre-k playground is nearing completion after a two week delay in July due to an electrical issue caused by the wiring feeding into the elementary building.  The issue was at no fault to the district and cost for upgrades have been covered by Ameren.  The district is planning having the pre-k students take part in a ribbon cutting when the playground officially opens this week.

In personnel matters the board hired Cameron Stone as a Title Teacher, Denise Phillips as Junior High School Cross Country Coach, and Mehgan Borcherding as High School Volleyball Freshman Coach.  They also hired Stephanie Coble as the Class of 2027 Sponsor, Noah Barnard as the Class of 2030 Sponsor, Morgan Cox as the High School “Nevco” Videoboard Sponsor, Rase Collins as Freshman Class Sponsor, Gavin Hosselton as High School Boys Basketball Fresh/Soph Coach, and Megan Welty as Junior High School Multi-Media Sponsor.  They also accepted the resignation of Mandi Bloemker as elementary teacher, effective immediately.

title: FLORA HYDRANT FLUSHING
full_story:
The City of Flora Water Department will have its fire hydrant flushing program on Wednesday, August 26th and 27th from 7:30 am until approximately 3:30 pm.

Although it may appear to be a waste of water, the process is part of a routine maintenance program necessary to maintain the integrity of the water system, allowing the city to continue to deliver the highest quality water possible to customers.  As a result of the line flushing process, residents in the immediate vicinity of the work may experience temporary discoloration of their water.  This discoloration consists primarily of harmless silt and air and does not affect the safety of the water.

If you experience discoloration in your water after crews have been flushing in your neighborhood, clear the pipes in your home by running all water faucets for a few minutes.  Washing light colored laundry is not recommended during this period.  The same philosophy of water line preventive maintenance is one that you should use in your own home to ensure the quality of water inside your home.  Your home’s water heater should be drained and flushed on a regular basis, according to manufacturers’ recommendations, to keep it working effectively and efficiently.

title: SHADOWS OF ELMWOOD
full_story:
Flora Rotary will be hosting its 12th annual Shadows of Elmwood Cemetery Tour on Friday, September 11th and Saturday, September 12th. Tickets will be available at the Flora Depot.

Ticket sales will start just before 5 pm with the first wagon leaving at 5 each night.  Tickets are sold until 9 pm and the wagons will go until the last patron has gone through.  Tickets are $8 each unless you purchase a Benefactor Ticket at $25 and go to the front of the line to get on the next available wagon.

The club will also have ride assist tickets for those unable to ride on the hay wagons.  If you are physically unable to ride the wagon, they will have spots available on golf carts that will follow the wagons through the cemetery.  Tickets are reserved for those who are in need, and available on a first come first served basis.

While you wait at the Depot there will be 2 additional skits to keep you entertained and there will be concessions available from Krazy Sweet Treats.

All proceeds from the cemetery tour go to Flora Rotary for their projects in the community.  The Rotary Club is currently working on updating Flora Rotary Park and adding improvements at Flora’s Pickleball Courts.

title: EFFINGHAM ARREST
full_story:
On Wednesday, the Effingham County Sheriff’s Office served an arrest warrant on 29-year-old Johnny A. Soto II, of Teutopolis, for multiple felony counts of production of Child Sexual Abuse Materials (CSAM).

Soto faces 7 Counts of Child Sexual Abuse Materials, all class 1 felonies; and 3 Counts of Child Sexual Abuse Materials, all class X felonies.

The arrest warrant stems from an investigation conducted by Detectives at the Effingham County Sheriff’s Office, which began earlier this year.

The Effingham County Sheriff’s Office was assisted by the Effingham Police Department, the Teutopolis Police Department, the Illinois State Police and the Effingham County State’s Attorney’s Office.

After Soto’s pretrial detention hearing on Friday, he was ordered to be detained at the Effingham County Jail.

The investigation into this matter remains ongoing at this time.

All suspects are to be considered innocent until proven guilty in a court of law.

title: INGRAHAM LABOR DAY PICNIC
full_story:

With an entry fee of $20.00, the truck pull begins at 9:00 am, followed by the modified, stock, diesel and tractor pulls at 1:00 pm, including the Illinois Stock Pullers Association, the Central Illinois Tractor Pullers Association, and the Illinois Hot Farm Stock Pullers, plus Stock Farm Class and Brush Class Semi Trucks, with the gate admission at $10.00 for adults and $5.00 for children age 6 to 12.

title: SKIPPING THE DMV
full_story:
Illinois Secretary of State Alexi Giannoulias is encouraging Illinoisans to join the growing number of customers skipping the DMV by completing routine driver and vehicle transactions through the Secretary of State’s online services.

Every day, up to 2,000 customers visit DMV facilities for driver and vehicle services that can be completed online thanks to the office’s ongoing modernization efforts.  Before making a trip, Illinoisans can visit www.ilsos.gov to see if their transaction can be handled online from home, work or on the go.

“Why take time out of your busy schedule to spend time at the DMV when you can get it done online?”  Giannoulias said.  “Most routine driver and vehicle services can be completed online in just a few minutes, from wherever you are.  If you can get it done online from your computer or from your phone, you can skip the trip, save yourself time and get back to the things that matter most.”

Over the past year, Illinoisans completed nearly 4.4 million online renewals of eligible driver’s licenses, state IDs and vehicle stickers, demonstrating the growing use of the Secretary of State’s online services.

During the first seven months of 2026, some 560,000 eligible driver’s license and ID transactions were completed online, compared with nearly 392,000 during the same period in 2025; a 43% increase.

The percentage of eligible driver’s license and ID transactions completed online also rose from approximately 14% during the first seven months of 2025 to 22% during the same period in 2026.

Vehicle sticker renewals have also continued to shift online.  During the first seven months of 2026, Illinoisans completed more than 2.25 million vehicle sticker renewals online, compared with nearly 2.17 million during the same period in 2025; a nearly 4% increase.

title: PERSON OF INTEREST NAMED
full_story:
Illinois State Police identified a person of interest in the kidnapping and murder of Iowa college student Tammy Zywicki, who was last seen alive 34-years ago on Interstate 80 in LaSalle County.

Marking the anniversary of Zywicki’s disappearance, State Police are asking the public for information about a woman who is not a suspect.  However, Theresa “Teri” Belenske was known to hitch hike and may have been traveling with an unknown trucker possibly responsible for Zywicki’s death.

Belenske, whose maiden name was Vega, died in 2014 at age 54.  She would have been 32 at the time of Zywicki’s death.

State Police said special agents are looking for information about Belenske from the late 1980s through the mid-1990s.  She has ties to several cities in California, including Oceanside, Vista, Pomona, San Bernadino, and Fontana.

Zywicki was last seen with her car, a 1985 white Pontiac T1000, on I-80 at mile marker 83, between 3:10 pm and 4 pm on August 23rd, 1992.  She left the Chicago suburb of Evanston for college in Grinnell, Iowa, where she was expected to arrive that evening.

A trooper found Zywicki’s abandoned vehicle, and her body was found September 1st, 1992, along Interstate 44 in rural Lawrence County, Missouri.  Authorities said she was stabbed to death.

A semi driver who reportedly was seen near Zywicki’s car was described as a white male, between 35 and 40-years-old, over 6 feet tall, with dark, bushy hair.

Anyone with information about the killing, or Belenske and who she was traveling with during the late 1980s and early 1990s can leave a crime tip on the Illinois State Police Investigative Tips page or by calling 1-800-CALL-FBI.

The FBI is also offering a reward of up to $50,000 for information leading to the identification of the person or persons responsible for the crime.

State Police said the case remains active with ISP and the FBI “exploring new leads, examining 200 pieces of evidence, and retesting items with modern DNA technology.”

title: SETTLEMENT MOVES FORWARD
full_story:
A federal court is on track to approve John Deere’s proposed right-to-repair settlement in an ongoing class-action lawsuit filed by farmers across the country sometime after the first of the year, after issuing an amended order of preliminary approval on Monday.  The court also denied a Missouri farmer’s request to file briefs in response to a review of the differences and similarities between the farmer settlement and another settlement Deere reached with the Federal Trade Commission.

The order on the farmer settlement was filed by the US District Court for the Northern District of Illinois a little more than one month after the company reached a settlement with the FTC and five states.

US District Judge Iain D. Johnston said in an order last Monday that the farmer settlement is “fair, reasonable, adequate and in the best interests of the settlement class” and that the settlement raises “no obvious reasons to doubt its fairness.”

The judge set August 28th, as the new deadline for beginning notification of the farmer settlement class.  That class is expected to include more than 200,000 members who purchased repair services from John Deere or its authorized US dealers between January 10th, 2018, and May 18th, 2026.

The new deadline for filing objections to the $99 million settlement is December 4th, and the deadline for filing claim forms is December 31st, followed by a fairness hearing on January 19th.
